scope: Read-only Architect/Inspector review of the PR203 post-merge audit and the proposed P4-02-S2 packet against merge 2df548e0. During the review the lane committed its work as a8336c43, so the committed versions were reviewed. Also read the uncommitted 23-line backlog.md addition and the untracked same-family-review.md and inventory-verification.json for context. Files reviewed: PR203-post-merge README and JSON receipts (pr, candidate/main/required checks, main-ci, trusted-rc history and log, audit-observe, preservation-start), P4-02-S2-approval-packet.md, P4-02-S2-owned-paths.json, and the updated plan, AUTHORIZATION, COMPLETION-PLAN, BUILD-PLAN, C-0003, backlog, rounds index, handoff and chain.json. Checked against ADR-0045/0047/0048/0049/0052, JW01-claim-wiring-contract, P4-02-deadlines-risk-api, P4-02-D8-D11 amendment (A1, including §2 ownership and §6 risk read), policy.ts, the deadlines vitest config, check-commands census and inf-rls census. All 247 owned-path entries were re-hashed against 2df548e0: existence and sha256 match for every entry, 0 mismatches. Receipts agree with the claims. All five required candidate contexts passed; stack-smoke was SKIPPED and is not counted as a pass. DETRAN CI run 39298941118 passed. Trusted-local-RC run 39298941092 failed with gh HTTP 404 and is kept separate from the fallback verified-local-rc success. The audit-observe artifact hashes match chain entry EV-ded4f5431f6737ad, YELLOW, readiness_promoting=false. The packet's transport, error codes, If-Match 400, limit max 50, CASE_POOL_UNRESOLVED/RISK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE/CLAIM_LEGACY_UNVERIFIED, v+2/v+1 legacy paths, NULL priority exclusion and A/C proposta rows all trace to accepted sources. The backend-only split keeps every T4–T6 and journey obligation, and no approval or completion is claimed.

findings.detail: S1 lifecycle state is still in the worktree, untracked: TASK-0028..0031 are 'ready' (backlog.jsonl says 'queued') and six S1 module locks have expired TTLs. Every record says S1 is integrated. EV-ded4f5431f6737ad lists these files as dirty_files, so the exact-merge observation ran on a dirty tree. The README's preservation section does not mention this S1 task/lock state.
findings.recommendation: Before any S2 task registration, close or release the S1 tasks and locks through the supported DEVAI lifecycle verbs, or record their custody explicitly. Do not hand-delete them. Then S2 IDs, locks and worktrees cannot collide with or inherit stale S1 state, and the next observation starts from a clean tree.

findings.detail: Section 2 (lines 17–31) still has a header calling it the current execution order. Its rows still say PR203 is a candidate pending merge (line 27) and that the next action is to check CI and merge PR203 (line 31). Its PC-tranche line also still lists PR203 as pending (line 132). findings.detail: The packet says both new GETs reuse existing permissions but does not name the @Resource/@Action pair. In policy.ts, claim-next is analyst-only (['rait-case','claim-next',['rait-analyst']]), while the scoped reads use @Resource('inf:rait-case') @Action('read'), which many roles hold. If raitClaimContext is decorated with 'read', or with a new action label, it would either widen access past the analyst claim permission or require editing policy.ts, which S2 does not own.
findings.recommendation: State the exact tuples: raitClaimContext uses @Resource('inf:rait-case') @Action('claim-next'), and raitCaseRiskSnapshot uses @Resource('inf:rait-case') @Action('read') plus the S1 parent/purpose predicate. Add an HTTP negative test showing a read-only role is denied claim-context.

findings.detail: ADR-0047 makes both claim-context and claim fail with CASE_POOL_UNRESOLVED409, and ADR-0049 makes both fail with RISK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE503. ADR-0048 only says a selector that cannot build its safe ordered set returns CLAIM_LEGACY_UNVERIFIED409. The packet does not say whether the selected-pool claim-context GET returns that 409 or a degraded queue page when an in-scope legacy row is unverified. Its acceptance list does not cover the GET either.
findings.recommendation: State the GET behavior explicitly; the most consistent reading is that the whole selected-pool context also returns 409. Add a GET case to the legacy acceptance bullet. If the sources do not decide it, record it as a bounded stop item instead of leaving it to the Engineer.

findings.detail: The WORKLIST harness runtime (createWorklistCommandRuntime) still handles 'claim-next' with DISTRIBUIDO-only selection and checks WIP before QUEUE_EMPTY, the reverse of the ADR-0045 §7 precedence S2 enforces. Its tests (rait-worklist-command-contract.spec.ts, rait-worklist-corrective.spec.ts) are neither owned by S2 nor disposed of. A second, contrary claim definition will remain after S2.
findings.recommendation: Record a disposition in the packet: either a legacy harness kept read-only, with a note that it is not the canonical claim contract, or a bounded owned change. Then reviewers will not treat its regressions as conflicting evidence.

findings.detail: backend/app/tests/e2e/rait-ctg2-final-structural.e2e.spec.ts uses the pool-scope fixtures. Its pool-provenance fixture needed repairs in S1 CI (de976582, e2391e65). S2 changes the owned rait-case-pool-scope.service.ts and adds legacy qualification, but this test is not in the inventory. Under the stop rule, a likely fixture update would pause S2 mid-flight, as happened with the RLS census before it was added.
findings.recommendation: Pre-classify it now: either an explicit read-only regression that must stay byte-identical, or a bounded Inspector-owned path with its baseline hash and an allowed-change statement.

findings.detail: The README says the observation ran 'as Auditor'. The chain entry EV-ded4f5431f6737ad records actor 'devai-cli' with actor_role 'harness'; the invocation used --as-role auditor.
findings.recommendation: Say that the CLI ran with --as-role auditor and the chain records actor_role=harness, so the receipt and the claim match exactly.

limitations: No tests, CI, generators, devai doctor or proof-chain verification were run. CI conclusions come only from the committed receipts.
